successful_milestone: Four matched native cases at dt=0.0025 completed with exact zero-source field equivalence (0 <= 1e-12) and 1004-element mesh. At t=0.03, e[2]-weighted opposing-lobe cancellation remains 73.54% negative / 75.79% positive, and R*e[2]-weighted cancellation 72.92% negative / 75.11%. This preserves a qualitative redistribution-like response through two timestep halvings; it does not prove current conservation or numerical convergence.
interpretation: The odd-symmetry residual fell from 80.11% at dt=0.01 to 57.12% at dt=0.005 and 35.94% at dt=0.0025 (latest -21.19 percentage points). However, negative cancellation shifted -6.46 percentage points, positive cancellation +1.40 points, and signed proxies remain materially timestep-dependent. Qualitative opposite-sign jphi lobes persist, but quantitative convergence is not established. A bounded fourth-level dt=0.00125 test with explicit convergence-difference ratios at matched physical times is justified.
followup_scope: One focused dt=0.00125 native M3D-C1 four-case refinement (24 steps to t=0.03) plus descriptive four-level dt=0.01/0.005/0.0025/0.00125 response-proxy difference ratios at aligned t=0.01,0.02,0.03. No solver physics, source profile, frozen thresholds or fidelity boundary changed.
